name: The dose keeps climbing and it stopped working
problem: I did everything they told me for years and it got worse, not better. The dose keeps going up and I have no idea where it ends.
golden_nugget: The only direction the number goes is up, and one day 'manage it' becomes 'remove it'.
source_quote: A few years ago, the laxatives stopped working… Now, I'm back where I was.
hook_seeds: You did everything right. So why is it getting worse?
notes: Absolution first, always. Never imply she under-tried. Compliance: never say addiction, dependency, tolerance or cathartic colon; the defensible villain is that laxatives treat the symptom without rebuilding the rhythm.

name: Flat at breakfast, unbuttoned by 2pm
problem: I am flat in the morning and by the afternoon my stomach is so distended I have to change out of what I put on.
golden_nugget: I dress every morning around a body I know is going to betray me by lunch.
source_quote: By the evening, tight clothes such as jeans have to be replaced by loose fitting clothing.
notes: PRODUCT TRUTH: route all de-bloat relief through regularity itself (less retained fermenting stool) plus gut-calming. No standalone de-bloat ingredient claim. Chlorophyll anti-bloat is unsupported and is out of the constipation formula.

name: Hours on the toilet for a pebble
problem: I sit and strain for the better part of an hour and get almost nothing, and the pain and pressure keep me awake afterwards.
golden_nugget: The most private, most basic thing a body does has turned into an hour of failing at it alone.
source_quote: I would push and push for hours, only to get a pea-sized amount out.
hook_seeds: Twenty minutes in there. For a pebble.
notes: Handle the bleeding/fissure evidence with care; it is real in the corpus but graphic. Keep it as her aftermath, never as a product claim.

name: The drug is finally working and it is the reason nothing moves
problem: The shot is the first thing that ever worked for my weight, and it is also the reason nothing has moved in days, and I am not willing to give it up.
golden_nugget: I finally got the thing I wanted and I am paying for it in a currency nobody warned me about.
source_quote: I like the results. But the cost of it is just too high.
hook_seeds: Nobody tells you the shot works by slowing your stomach down.
notes: Canonical mechanism for this avatar is TOP NOT BOTTOM (2026-08-17): the problem is the slowed stomach, everything she has tried works at the colon. Do not carry v3 signal/conveyor-belt language or the MiraLAX-dementia beat.

name: The belly cancels out the weight loss
problem: I have lost real weight and my stomach still looks the way it did, so the one thing I wanted to see is the one thing nobody can see.
golden_nugget: I bought the body back and the mirror still shows me the old one.
source_quote: She is finally 'skinny' (or getting there), but she feels grosser than when she was fat.
notes: PRODUCT TRUTH: same as MOT-A-002, relief routes through regularity only. Never imply Motilli affects weight loss or GLP-1 efficacy.

name: Looking pregnant, and the shame of it
cohort: women whose afternoon distension visibly reads as pregnancy to other people
self_id_line: If you have ever put a hand over your stomach in a photo because you knew what it looked like, this is for you.
problem: By the afternoon my stomach sticks out so far that I look pregnant, and I spend the rest of the day making sure nobody looks at it or says anything about it.
golden_nugget: At my age, looking pregnant is not a compliment. It is a thing I have to explain, or hide, and I would rather hide.
source_quote: I feel pregnant,' or even 'I look pregnant,' are frequent complaints
hook_seeds: Flat this morning. Six months along by 2pm.
I stopped standing sideways in photographs.
notes: The 'when are you due' beat is DRAMATISED, not in the corpus. The sourced version is that she says she looks and feels pregnant and changes clothes. If a script uses a stranger asking, mark it as a creative choice, not a testimonial. PRODUCT TRUTH: relief routes through regularity only.

name: Lost the weight, still asked about the belly
cohort: women months into a GLP-1 whose scale has moved but whose stomach still reads pregnant
self_id_line: If the scale has moved thirty pounds and your stomach has not moved at all, it is not the fat that is still there.
problem: I have lost real weight on this and my stomach still looks six months pregnant, so nobody can see what I have actually done.
golden_nugget: I paid for this with nausea and needles and I still cannot wear the thing I bought it for.
source_quote: The Bloating Makes Me Look Like I Haven't Lost Any Weight
source: brands/motilli/celery juice gummies/research/docs/avatar - GLP1 constipation (women)/Avatar Research - GLP1 Constipation (Women).md#L61
notes: INFERRED: the source is a research theme title synthesising community language, not a captured quote. Pull one verbatim line from a GLP-1 group before this goes HIGH. Never imply Motilli affects weight loss.

name: It started the year my cycle stopped
cohort: women whose constipation began with the menopause transition around 50
self_id_line: If you can name the year this started, and it is the same year your period stopped, that is not a coincidence you imagined.
problem: I was regular my whole life until my cycle stopped around fifty, and it has never gone back, and no one has ever connected the two for me.
golden_nugget: Everything about my body changed at once and this is the part I was never warned about and cannot say out loud.
source_quote: chronic constipation ever since my menstrual cycle stopped around age 50, and I'm now approaching 58
hook_seeds: It started the year your cycle stopped. Nobody told you those were connected.
notes: COMPLIANCE: keep the hormone mechanism vague and associative. Use the epidemiology (constipation runs 2-3x higher in older women) and never assert 'your estrogen dropped and slowed your colon' - the literature contradicts itself. Do not cite the 54% peri/menopause figure, it traces to a low-authority source.

name: The fiber everyone swears by made it worse
cohort: women who added the recommended fiber and got harder, drier, more bloated
self_id_line: If the fiber everyone swears by is the thing that dried you up, you were not doing it wrong.
problem: I took the fiber everyone recommends and it made me harder and more bloated, and I could not believe it because it works for everybody else.
golden_nugget: When the universal advice fails on you, you stop blaming the advice and start believing you are the broken one.
source_quote: I found that taking Metamucil dried up my stool and gave me constipation
hook_seeds: The fiber everyone swears by is making you harder, not softer.
It was the wrong kind of fiber, not the wrong amount.
notes: WORDING LAW: the villain is coarse bran-type bulk fiber, never 'fiber supplements' broadly and never psyllium/Metamucil by name in copy - psyllium is soluble and the best-evidenced fiber for constipation. Her quote can stay hers; our claim cannot name the brand. Motilli's fiber is a deliberate prebiotic micro-dose.

name: Rationing her own laxatives out of fear
cohort: women who hold back from stronger laxatives because they are afraid of where it ends
self_id_line: If you have sat there deciding whether to take the second dose, because of what taking it might mean, you already know what this is about.
problem: I am scared to take more even when the dose I am on is not working, because the last thing I want is to need it forever.
golden_nugget: I am not frightened of today. I am frightened of the version of me who needs four of these a day and has no next step.
source_quote: the last thing I want is to become dependent on laxatives
hook_seeds: You are not scared of today's dose. You are scared of next year's.
notes: HARD COMPLIANCE LINE: this angle voices HER fear, it never asserts the claim. Never say laxatives are addictive, cause dependency or damage the colon - ACG/AGA treat that as a myth and it is FTC risk. Answer the fear structurally instead: this works at a different place, so it is not another rung on the same ladder. Every claim needs a demo beat.

name: Afraid of the bowel movement itself
cohort: women who have started dreading going because of what it costs them afterwards
self_id_line: If you brace yourself before you go, and then pay for it for hours afterwards, you are not being dramatic.
problem: I panic before I go now, because the pain afterwards lasts for hours and I know it is coming.
golden_nugget: I have become afraid of my own body doing the one thing it is supposed to do, and there is nobody I can say that to.
source_quote: I would panic before I went… in extreme pain for up to 8 hours after each BM. I was afraid of living.
hook_seeds: You do not dread the constipation. You dread the going.
notes: Handle without medicalising her. Never name it a phobia, never suggest it is psychological - the corpus shows she already fears being told it is in her head. No pain-relief claim: Motilli is structure/function only.

name: Told to eat 30g of fiber on an appetite she does not have
cohort: women on a GLP-1 told to hit 25-30g of fiber a day while barely finishing one meal
self_id_line: If the advice is a cup of broccoli with every meal, and you are not eating every meal, that advice was not written for you.
problem: Everyone tells me to eat more fiber, but the whole point of this medication is that I cannot eat much, so the advice is impossible before I even start.
golden_nugget: The fix everyone hands me requires the appetite the drug took away, which means nobody advising me has thought about my situation for ten seconds.
source_quote: Make sure to get 25 to 30 grams of fiber a day with enough water. I eat a cup of broccoli with every meal.
source: brands/motilli/celery juice gummies/research/docs/avatar - GLP1 constipation (women)/Avatar Research - GLP1 Constipation (Women).md#L104
hook_seeds: Thirty grams of fiber a day. On an appetite the shot took away.
notes: This is the cleanest entry for the prebiotic micro-dose pillar. DOSE CHECKPOINT: if per-serving fiber is well under ~5g, claim 'feeds beneficial gut bacteria' only, never 'clinically speeds transit' or 'increases bowel movements'. Also: eating more is not the answer we sell, so avoid any beat that reads as diet advice.

name: Planning the day around a bathroom
cohort: women who time remedies and map bathrooms before they will leave the house
self_id_line: If you have ever picked the remedy by how fast it works so it does not catch you out somewhere, you plan your life around this.
problem: I choose what to take by how quickly it works, because I cannot risk it kicking in when I am out, so my whole day gets built around a bathroom.
golden_nugget: My world has quietly shrunk to the places I know I can get to a bathroom in time, and I never announced that to anyone.
source_quote: work in 15 minutes so you don't have to worry about it kicking in when out of the house
source: brands/motilli/celery juice gummies/research/docs/avatar - GLP1 constipation (women)/Avatar Research - GLP1 Constipation (Women).md#L149
hook_seeds: You do not pick it by how well it works. You pick it by how fast.
notes: Strong travel and social-plans territory. Results must be shown as life moments restored (saying yes to dinner without mapping the bathrooms), never as clinical metrics.

name: Not telling the doctor the whole truth
cohort: women who under-report side effects because they are afraid of losing the prescription
self_id_line: If you have edited what you told your doctor so they would not take it away from you, you are not the only one.
problem: I hold back how bad it actually is at my appointments, because if I say it out loud they will take me off the one thing that finally worked.
golden_nugget: I am managing my own doctor to protect a drug that is hurting me, and that is not a position I ever expected to be in.
source_quote: If I tell my doctor about the vomiting, she'll take me off Wegovy. I can't go back to the hunger.
hook_seeds: You told your doctor it was manageable. It is not manageable.
notes: SAFETY LINE: name the behaviour, never encourage it. Copy must not say or imply keep it from your doctor. The turn is: you should not have to choose between telling the truth and keeping the medication.

name: Fifteen months in, it never became temporary
cohort: women a year or more into a GLP-1 for whom the side effect never settled down
self_id_line: If you were told this settles down after a few weeks, and you are counting in months now, nobody prepared you for this part.
problem: They said this part would pass in a few weeks. I am over a year in and the last eight months have been the worst of it.
golden_nugget: I have started doing the maths on whether being this size is worth this, and I hate that I am even asking.
source_quote: I've been on it for 15 months and the past 8 months it's been too much
hook_seeds: They told you it settles down after a few weeks. You are counting in months.
notes: The long-hauler is a different buyer from the week-three newbie: she has already run the whole remedy cocktail and is cynical. Lead with the mechanism reveal, not with reassurance. Never suggest stopping or adjusting her medication.
